citations.narrative:
In three enclosures, housing a total of three adult dogs and sixteen puppies, the dog food in the bowls and self-feeders is
heavily contaminated with wood shavings. The food in several receptacles is almost completely buried under the shavings
which increases the risk of inadvertent consumption of the shavings when the dogs are trying to eat the food. Failure of
the facility to keep the food uncontaminated could have serious negative impacts on the health of the dogs.
Dogs must be fed at least once each day, except as otherwise might be required to provide adequate veterinary care. The
food must be uncontaminated, wholesome, palatable, and of sufficient quantity and nutritive value to maintain the normal
condition and weight of the animal. The facility must ensure that the food in the bowls and self-feeders remains free of
wood shavings and any other contaminates, in order to support the health and well-being of the dogs.
Correction date: October 7, 2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representative.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
